curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8257-1/ (scans of two books; the file builds both main models, facing each other: book 1, the purple tracked striker, is scans 001-027, its pages 1-27 (scan 005 repeats page 4, so page 5 is missing), and its alternate models follow in scans 028-046; book 2, the teal wheeled striker, is scans 047-075, its pages 1-29; scans 076-077 are the sticker sheets)

functions.does: The purple striker runs on two rubber tracks, each round three yellow sprocket wheels that turn freely on their axles. Nothing drives them: it's pushed along the floor by its handle.
functions.source: book 1: steps 10-11; page 27 shows it pushed back and forth

functions.does: Pulling the purple striker's trigger, the yellow towball arm under the top of its handle, swings the block that the back end of the scissor arm is pinned to. The scissor arm (lazy tongs of purple and black thin beams) then shoots forward, with the rubber-tipped arrow at its tip, at the other striker's target.
functions.source: book 1: steps 12-19 (the trigger block; the scissor arm, built in its own steps 1-5, is fitted in step 17), page 27 panel 2 (the arm shot out); inferred: the book draws no arrow on the trigger itself

functions.does: The purple striker's seat sits on a lever pivoted at the top of its handle: a black cage with purple hoses that holds the driver. The seat flips forward and throws the driver off. Pushed back down, it clicks into the catch at the top of the target lever.
functions.source: book 1: steps 22 (the lever and its shock absorber), 27 (the seat, built in its own steps 1-6) and 28 (the driver put in; CLICK as it latches), page 26 panels 2-4, page 27 panel 2
functions.note: The driver only sits in the cage, so in play he flies off when the seat flips (page 27 panel 2). inferred: that the seat is fixed to the lever (a single axle 4 joins them in step 27).

functions.does: Hitting the purple striker's target swings the target lever back on its pivot under the seat. The target is a disc on the end of that purple lever, low at the front. The lever's top end is the catch that holds the seat down, so the seat is let go and flips forward. The other striker's arrow aims at this target.
functions.source: book 1: steps 23-26 (step 26 shows the lever pulled back and the seat's lever swinging up), page 26 panel 2, page 27 panel 2
functions.note: Only the spring flips the seat, once the catch lets go (see the shock absorbers below). Dragging the target lever alone shouldn't move the seat.

functions.does: The teal striker runs on three wheels that roll freely: one at the front, under the target, and two on an axle under the handle. Nothing drives them: it's pushed along the floor by its handle.
functions.source: book 2: steps 8 and 12; book 1 page 27 shows it pushed back and forth

functions.does: Pulling the teal striker's trigger, the yellow towball arm under the top of its handle, shoots its scissor arm out at the other striker, just as on the purple one. The arm is teal and black, with a rubber-tipped arrow at its tip.
functions.source: book 2: steps 12-19 (the trigger block; the scissor arm, built in its own steps 1-5, is fitted in step 17), book 1 page 27 panel 2; inferred: the book draws no arrow on the trigger itself

functions.does: The teal striker's seat is a cage of grey angle connectors and axles round the driver, with a screen tile, on a lever pivoted at the top of its handle. It flips forward and throws the driver off. Pushed back down, it clicks into the catch at the top of the target lever.
functions.source: book 2: steps 22 (the lever and its shock absorber), 27-28 (the cage) and 29 (the driver put in; CLICK as it latches); book 1 page 26 shows how it's worked
functions.note: The driver only sits in the cage, so in play he flies off when the seat flips (book 1 page 27 panel 2). inferred: that the cage is fixed to the lever.

functions.does: Hitting the teal striker's target swings the target lever back on its pivot under the seat. The target is a disc on the end of that teal lever, low at the front. The lever's top end is the catch that holds the seat down, so the seat is let go and flips forward.
functions.source: book 2: steps 23-26 (step 26 shows the lever pulled back and the seat's lever swinging up); book 1 page 26 panel 2
functions.note: Only the spring flips the seat, once the catch lets go (see the shock absorbers below). Dragging the target lever alone shouldn't move the seat.

functions.does: On each striker, a spring shock absorber between the seat's lever and the handle flips the seat forward as soon as the target lets go of it. Pushing the seat back down compresses it again.
functions.source: book 1: step 22, page 26 panel 2; book 2: step 22
functions.skip: a spring, which only matters under force; the seats swing by hand without it

functions.does: On each striker, two rubber bands pull the trigger back, which folds the scissor arm away again when the trigger is let go.
functions.source: book 1: step 20; book 2: step 20; inferred: where they hook on, from the model file (round the towball pins behind the trigger block)
functions.skip: the rubber bands only pull; the arm folds back by hand without them

questions.question: Is the 6572 the trigger, and is the seat fixed to its lever?
